title: LEGO Star Wars Magazine Issue 141 Includes Free Death Trooper Minifigure

bodyMarkdown:

For LEGO Star Wars army builders, magazine giveaways offer a cheaper route to bulking out troop ranks compared to buying full battle packs. At £5.99 versus £17.99 for the retiring battle pack, this is a notable saving for collectors chasing specific minifigures.

title: Fan builder turns LEGO Dolphins set into a Millennium Falcon MOC

bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Fan designer creationcaravan4 (Brad Barber) has revealed his 20th custom take on the Millennium Falcon, this time reimagined using pieces from LEGO Creator 3-in-1 set 31385 Beautiful Dolphins. The build, nicknamed the Millennium Dolphin and Y-Wing, turns the 542-piece set into a pair of aquatic-themed ships, complete with an undersea display stand and a curved wave element supporting the main model.

This follows the creator's earlier Slowpoke MOC, built entirely from a single copy of 43306 Lotso with no extra parts. It's unclear yet whether the Millennium Dolphin build also uses only pieces from the original set, as full details haven't been shared. Instructions are said to be coming soon via Rebrickable.

Previous entries in this long-running MOC series have reworked sets including 40872 Pumpkin Lantern, 77260 Fast & Furious Toyota Supra MK4, and 43032 FIFA World Cup 2026 Official Emblem into Falcon-style builds.

## Why it matters
This is a fun example of how versatile LEGO Creator 3-in-1 sets can be in the hands of skilled fan builders, showing that a single retail set can be transformed into something wildly different from its intended designs. It's a great reminder for MOC fans and Bricks in a Bag customers of the creative potential hiding in ordinary parts.

## What to watch next

For Lord of the Rings LEGO fans priced out of the original Tower of Orthanc, this offers an affordable and creative alternative using a set that's still readily available. title: LEGO Star Wars ditches the cone: IG-88 gets a brand new minifigure head
summary: LEGO designers have confirmed that the upcoming UCS Executor Super Star Destroyer introduces a purpose-built head element for IG-88, replacing the classic upturned cone used since 2006.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
According to Brick Fanatics, the design team behind LEGO Star Wars set 75457 UCS Executor Super Star Destroyer has revealed why IG-88's minifigure finally gets a new head piece. Since his debut in 2006's 6209 Slave I, IG-88 has been built using a simple upside-down 1x1 cone combined with cylinders or round plates - a look also used for other assassin droids like IG-11 right up until 2025.

Speaking to Brick Fanatics and other LEGO fan media, lead designer John Ho said he'd "been screaming for" an upgrade because he "really don't like the cone". Graphic designer Madison O'Neil added that the team worked closely with LEGO's element designers to create a new piece "optimised for decoration", balancing enough LEGO "DNA" without going overboard.

The new specialist head element appears with different printing in both 75457 UCS Executor Super Star Destroyer and 75456 Star Wars Advent Calendar, covering IG-88 and IG-11 respectively. The Executor set is confirmed to release on 1 October.

## Why it matters
This is a nice example of how LEGO's UCS teams can influence wider System-level element design - a new head piece created for one flagship set can end up shaping how droid characters look across the whole LEGO Star Wars range going forward. For collectors and minifigure fans, it means older cone-head assassin droid figures may start to look dated compared to future releases.

## What to watch next
Designers have hinted this new head tool will be used for other assassin droids in future sets, so keep an eye out for updated IG-series or similar droid minifigures beyond 75457 and 75456.

title: Last-ever Hampshire Brick Event to sell off rare LEGO collection
summary: The long-running Hampshire Brick Event is holding its final edition on 10 October, with organiser Ty selling off much of his personal LEGO collection, including rarities and retired sets.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
After more than a decade of running, the Hampshire Brick Event on the south coast of England will hold its last-ever edition on 10 October. According to Brick Fanatics, organiser and collector Ty will be selling off the majority of his personal LEGO collection built up over the past ten years or so, including some unusual and hard-to-find items not typically seen on the aftermarket, alongside rare, retired and boxed sets.

The event will also feature the usual mix that fans have come to expect: a LEGO-themed goody bag for attendees while stocks last, a free spin on a prize draw for LEGO-themed hampers, a loose brick buying area, a table of freebies such as posters and old instructions, display stands, select MOCs, LEGO-themed t-shirts for sale, and a lucky dip with prizes including a set of five AT-ATs and buckets of loose LEGO.

Iain's Bricks will return with sets for sale, and the organiser will also have a table selling off part of their own collection, including some retired sets, though on a smaller scale than a previous clear-out that reportedly drew large crowds.

## Why it matters
